sections.body: Ask about the entrance, photos, quiet behavior, and the local cathedral name before stepping inside.

sections.title: Facade First
sections.body: Take the street view before worrying about the interior. If the doors are open, lower your voice and let the room decide how long you stay.

sections.title: The Rooster Name Cue
sections.body: Nha tho Con Ga is the local name many people recognize. It is handy for drivers, maps, and hearing it around town.

sections.title: Worship Space Stays Clear
sections.body: Avoid blocking aisles, doors, or services. The building can be a landmark and still ask for quiet guest behavior.

entries.summary: A practical Da Nang transport handoff where bags, bays, route signs, fare questions, and the next road matter more than scenery on the day.
entries.context: For travel days when the visitor needs to match the vehicle, route, bay, and exit plan without burning patience.
entries.tip: Save the station name, next stop, and hotel address in Vietnamese. Showing the screen can be cleaner than repeating tones near engines.
entries.rationale: The bus station gives travel days a clearer script: confirm the bay, board the right vehicle, and plan the exit before arrival.

sections.title: Next Leg Before The Curb
sections.body: Da Nang Central Bus Station matters on practical days: bags at your feet, signs overhead, route details on your phone, and one more road ahead.

sections.title: Travel-Day Clarity
sections.body: This stop is about luggage, route signs, vehicle bays, and the next road. Confirm the practical pieces while patience and phone battery still exist.

sections.title: Bus Station Words
sections.body: Ask for the bay, route, ticket, next stop, luggage spot, and exit plan before boarding.

sections.title: Check The Bay Twice
sections.body: A city name on a sign is not enough. Bay, company, and direction all deserve a second look before boarding.

sections.title: Names On Screen
sections.body: Have the station name, next stop, and hotel address ready to show. A clear screen can beat uncertain pronunciation beside luggage carts.

sections.title: Exit Plan Early
sections.body: Decide how you will leave before the bus pulls in. Pickup point, taxi queue, or ride pin is easier with battery and patience intact.

entries.summary: A calm downtown culture stop where Cham sandstone, repeated forms, and the My Son, Tra Kieu, and Dong Duong rooms make Da Nang feel older.
entries.context: Good when the riverfront feels all speed and lights, and the visitor wants a slower historical layer in the middle of town.
entries.tip: Pick three rooms first, then look for dancers, deities, animals, altars, and carved movement before reading every label.
entries.rationale: The museum gives central Vietnam human historical texture in a compact visit, without needing the whole day.

sections.title: Three Rooms Before Labels
sections.body: The Museum of Cham Sculpture is easier with a small route. Begin with My Son, Tra Kieu, and Dong Duong, then let the stone slow you down.

sections.title: Stone First
sections.body: The sandstone can do the first explanation. The rooms make more sense after your eye adjusts to repeated poses, jewelry, animals, and temple fragments.

sections.title: Patterns Teach Fast
sections.body: Notice dancers in motion, steady-faced deities, lions, makaras, altars, and pieces from larger Cham sites. Pattern teaches faster than label-chasing.

sections.title: Downtown Counterweight
sections.body: The museum sits close enough to the Han River and Dragon Bridge to pair with a walk. It changes the pace before the waterfront returns.

entries.summary: A cold Da Nang dessert cup of jelly, coconut milk, shaved ice, chewy red cubes, and texture more than simple sweetness after heat.
entries.context: Good as a small cool-down after market snacks, a river walk, or a meal that needs a sweet finish.
entries.tip: Stir once before judging it. Coconut, ice, jelly, and syrup shift as the cup settles.
entries.rationale: Che xoa xoa hat luu gives Da Nang a quick sweet memory built around cold texture, not a heavy dessert stop.

sections.title: Texture Before Sweetness
sections.body: Che xoa xoa hat luu is a cold Da Nang dessert cup: jelly, coconut milk, shaved ice, syrup, and chewy red cubes.

sections.title: Cold Texture Stop
sections.body: This dessert makes sense as a small cool-down. Jelly, coconut, shaved ice, syrup, and chewy red pieces matter more than simple sweetness.

sections.title: Dessert Cup Words
sections.body: Ask for one dessert cup, less ice, less sugar, coconut, and the price before judging the texture.

sections.title: Stir, Then Taste
sections.body: The cup changes as coconut, ice, jelly, and syrup mix. The pleasure is soft, cold, slippery, and chewy at once.

sections.title: Red Cubes Are The Cue
sections.body: Hat luu means pomegranate seeds, but in this dessert the red pieces are usually chewy starch or jelly. Expect texture, not fruit.

sections.title: A Small Cool-Down
sections.body: Do not turn it into a search for one ideal cup. The pleasure is quick, cold, local-feeling, and easy to fold into the evening.

entries.summary: A casual Da Nang meal stop where the best move is one clear house dish, a menu read, and a little staff guidance before ordering the table.
entries.context: Good when dinner needs focus rather than a broad menu crawl, especially if duck, noodles, or a house plate brought you here.
entries.tip: Pick one main thing first. A simple first order keeps the meal readable before sides and second guesses arrive.
entries.rationale: Co Chu Nho feels most useful when the meal starts with a clear recommendation, spice level, and one focused first dish.

sections.title: One House Dish First
sections.body: Co Chu Nho works better as a focused casual dinner than a broad menu crawl. Read the menu, ask what is recommended, then order one main thing.

sections.title: One Main Thing
sections.body: The meal needs one center: duck, noodles, or a house plate. Staff guidance can narrow the first order.

sections.title: House Dish Words
sections.body: Ask what the house recommends, then order one main dish, spice level, sides, and the bill clearly.

sections.title: Menu Before Momentum
sections.body: Do not treat the meal like fuel between sights. Take a minute, notice what repeats, and ask before adding extra plates.

sections.title: Duck Or Noodles First
sections.body: If duck or noodles brought you here, let that guide the first decision. The table gets easier once the main order is clear.

sections.title: A Simple First Order
sections.body: A focused first dish is better than chasing the whole menu. Ask what the house recommends, then add only if the table still wants more.
